title: Federated Learning in Quantum Computing for Privacy-Preserving and Distributed Quantum Model Training
journal_or_venue: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Data Intelligence and Cognitive Informatics (ICDICI-2025), IEEE
abstract_summary: The paper proposes PQFL, a privacy-preserving federated learning framework for quantum machine learning that integrates Quantum Homomorphic Encryption (QHE) for secure aggregation and Quantum Differential Privacy (QDP) via quantum noise channels to limit information leakage. Hybrid quantum-classical simulations show PQFL achieves competitive accuracy compared with centralized QML while providing formal privacy guarantees and modest communication and qubit overheads, making it suitable for sensitive domains like healthcare and finance.
methodology_description: The paper proposes PQFL (Privacy-preserving Quantum Federated Learning), a hybrid quantum-classical federated learning framework. Multiple clients each train a local parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) model on their private local dataset by encoding classical inputs into quantum states via an encoding circuit E(x) and applying a parameterized unitary U(θ). Outputs are obtained by measuring an observable and computing a loss (MSE for binary classification). Gradients are estimated with the parameter-shift rule, and local parameters are updated with classical optimizers (SGD or Adam). To enforce privacy, clients add calibrated quantum noise (quantum Gaussian noise channel or discrete Pauli/depolarizing channels) to their local parameter deltas to achieve (ε, δ)-Quantum Differential Privacy. Noisy updates are then encrypted using a Quantum Homomorphic Encryption (QHE) scheme. The central aggregator performs homomorphic aggregation of encrypted updates and broadcasts the aggregated ciphertext; clients locally decrypt to obtain the averaged update and apply it to the global model for the next round. Experiments are performed in hybrid quantum-classical simulation environments using Python quantum libraries to evaluate accuracy, privacy leakage (ε), communication overhead, and qubit utilization across three configurations: centralized QML baseline, PQFL without QDP, and PQFL with QDP enabled.
algorithms_used: Quantum Homomorphic Encryption (QHE) for encrypted aggregation
Quantum Differential Privacy (QDP) via quantum Gaussian noise and depolarizing/Pauli channels
experimental_setup: Hybrid quantum-classical simulation using Python quantum libraries (Qiskit, PennyLane, TensorFlow Quantum). Simulations evaluate three configurations: centralized QML, PQFL without QDP, PQFL with QDP. Metrics recorded per communication round include accuracy, privacy loss (ε), communication overhead (KB), and qubit utilization (%). No specific QPU hardware or shot counts are reported.
experiment_process: Pipeline: (1) Server initializes global parameters θ_t and broadcasts to N clients. (2) Each client i encodes local data x_k^(i) into quantum state |ψ_k> via E(x) and runs PQC U(θ_it) to produce |φ_k(θ)>. (3) Measure observable to get predictions y^k and compute loss L_i (MSE for classification). (4) Compute gradients ∇_θ L_i using the parameter-shift rule and update local parameters: θ_i,t+1 = θ_i,t − η ∇_θ L_i (optimizer SGD/Adam). (5) Compute local delta Δθ_i,t = θ_i,t+1 − θ_i,t. (6) Apply Quantum Differential Privacy: add quantum Gaussian noise N_Q(0,σ^2) or apply depolarizing/Pauli noise channel to produce noisy Δθ_i,t~. (7) Encrypt noisy update with QHE: E_QHE(Δθ_i,t~). (8) Send encrypted updates to server; server homomorphically aggregates ∑_i E_QHE(Δθ_i,t~) leveraging linearity of QHE. (9) Server broadcasts aggregated ciphertext; clients decrypt locally to obtain averaged update and set θ_{t+1} = θ_t + (1/N) ∑_i Δθ_i,t~. (10) Repeat for multiple federated rounds. Parameters reported: privacy budget ε (set to 1.2 in experiments), learning rate η (unspecified), noise variance σ^2 (not specified), depolarizing probability p (not quantified, described as correlated with ε). Number of rounds, shots, circuit depth and number of qubits per experiment are not specified beyond qubit-utilization percentages.
experiment_output: Reported metrics: classification accuracy (%) for each configuration (Centralized QML: 91.4%, PQFL no QDP: 90.1%, PQFL with QDP: 88.7%); privacy loss ε reported for QDP-enabled run (ε = 1.2); communication overhead per round in KB (Centralized: 850 KB, PQFL no QDP: 920 KB, PQFL with QDP: 960 KB); qubit utilization percentages (Centralized: 75%, PQFL no QDP: 72%, PQFL with QDP: 70%). Baseline: centralized QML model. Outputs are aggregated performance statistics per configuration; no per-round learning curves, standard deviations, or statistical tests are provided.

results_summary: The paper introduces PQFL, a federated learning architecture for quantum machine learning that combines Quantum Homomorphic Encryption for encrypted aggregation and Quantum Differential Privacy via noise channels. In hybrid simulations the authors report that PQFL achieves accuracy close to a centralized quantum model (91.4% centralized vs. 90.1% PQFL without QDP; 88.7% with QDP at ε=1.2), with modest increases in per-round communication overhead (850 KB → 920–960 KB) and small reductions in reported qubit utilization (75% → 70–72%). The authors present PQFL as a privacy-enhancing, modular approach suitable for sensitive application domains, while noting trade-offs between privacy and utility.

key_ideas: #idea:hybrid-approach — PQFL presents a hybrid quantum-classical federated learning pipeline: local PQCs trained with parameter-shift gradients and classical optimizers, encrypted aggregation via Quantum Homomorphic Encryption (QHE), and Quantum Differential Privacy (QDP) applied through quantum noise channels.

#idea:near-term-feasibility — Hybrid simulations (Qiskit/PennyLane/TFQ) report competitive accuracy close to a centralized QML baseline (91.4% vs 90.1% PQFL without QDP), and authors argue modest communication/qubit overheads, positioning PQFL as applicable to sensitive domains including finance and healthcare.
#limitation:simulation-only — All experiments are performed in classical hybrid simulators with no real QPU experiments, no shot counts, and no hardware-specific evaluation reported.

#limitation:qubit-count — The paper does not specify absolute qubit counts or circuit depths (only reports qubit-utilization percentages), preventing assessment of real-device feasibility and scalability.
#limitation:data-encoding — Data encoding is performed via encoding circuits E(x) but encoding cost, scaling, and its impact on performance are not quantified.

#limitation:noise — While QDP injects calibrated quantum noise for privacy, the work does not evaluate the impact of real-device noise or apply error-mitigation strategies; hardware error impacts remain unassessed.

#idea:hybrid-approach — The approach integrates QHE for encrypted aggregation and client-side local decryption, enabling privacy-preserving federated updates without exposing raw data or cleartext parameter deltas to the server.
contradictions: The paper claims PQFL is suitable for sensitive domains including finance, but only compares PQFL to a centralized QML baseline (quantum baseline) and does not benchmark against classical ML/federated-learning baselines; the claimed practical advantage over classical approaches is therefore unsubstantiated.

The authors report 'modest' qubit and communication overheads yet omit concrete experimental parameters (absolute qubit counts, circuit depth, shot counts, number of clients/rounds and several hyperparameters), which contradicts the implication that the approach's scalability and immediate practicality are demonstrated.
